task: Fix the shared-worktree concurrent-build hazard that corrupts dist: add a cross-platform build mutex and make the build skip decision content-bound instead of mtime/existence.
outcome: Concurrent npm test invocations in one worktree never corrupt dist (no ENOTEMPTY/TS2307/MODULE_NOT_FOUND); a live long-running build is never age-stolen from its lock, a dead holder is reclaimed race-free, and builds skip only when a content-hash binding proves dist matches source.
facts: The build currently has NO lock (B-fb7b reverted scripts/build-lock.mjs after Codex found it buggy).

scripts/full-suite-build-binding.mjs already exports verifyBuildBinding/writeBuildBinding/treeDigest: sha256 over all packages/main src+tsconfig+package.json (sourceDigest) and all packages/main/dist (distDigest).
proper-lockfile is a pure-JS cross-platform lock (mkdir strategy + mtime heartbeat) that works on Mac/Linux/Windows.

There are three distinct build call sites: scripts/ensure-dist.mjs (the pretest), scripts/build-main-with-binding.mjs (which IS the packages-main-build validate command via npm --prefix packages/main run build), and the packages/utils build (tsc).
packages/utils tsc links against packages/main/dist, so utils freshness depends on main/dist too.
constraints: Cross-platform (Mac/Linux/Windows) — proper-lockfile, not POSIX-only flock (which would need a native module).
No atomic-publish/symlink dist-swap (YAGNI; Windows symlink perms fragile).
Touch only build infrastructure per the enforce scope contract.
unknowns: DEV-time detail: exact proper-lockfile stale/update interval config (stale>=30s, update<stale/2) to guarantee a live holder is never age-stolen.
DEV-time detail: the shape of the packages/utils build-binding manifest and where its sourceDigest incorporates the packages/main/dist it links against.
